description: Shared HAProxy contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server (server issue #494). Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/haproxy_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_haproxy.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip (only the socket/HTTP transport is mocked -- each scenario's 'raw_lines' are joined into the CSV that _socket_show_stat/_http_show_stat would return, and the 'capped_tick' scenario shrinks _SERVER_CAP to 'server_cap' so the cap can be exercised without synthesising 400+ rows). haproxy_metrics(**scenario['config']) must equal scenario['payload']. The server's spec/requests/api_collect_haproxy_spec.rb posts scenario['payload'] under data['haproxy'] through /collect and asserts Ingesters::Agent ingests each shape (list / capped-wrapper / [] / null). 'config' is the only field the server reads; 'raw_lines' and 'server_cap' are agent-side inputs the server ignores. Change the payload shape only in lockstep across both repos, keeping the two copies byte-identical.
_agent_min_version_note: PATCH on the 1.14.x release train (user-assigned): 1.14.0 = Docker image-inventory (issue #101), 1.14.1 = TSDB (issue #103), 1.14.3 = HAProxy (issue #105), 1.14.4 = Memcached (issue #106). HAProxy has NO server version gate (no FEATURES_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS entry -- it is purely config-driven, haproxy_enabled defaults false), so nothing gates on this number and a PATCH is fine; it is reconciled at merge/ship time.
null_contract: data['haproxy'] is one of FOUR shapes and the server MUST branch on them: (a) null (JSON null / Python None) = COLLECTION FAILURE -- the stats socket was refused/timed out, the HTTP CSV request failed / returned non-200, or the body was not parseable stats CSV. The server MUST NOT prune haproxy rows or auto-resolve haproxy_backend_down incidents on null: an unreachable HAProxy is not 'every backend recovered', and treating it as recovery is a false-resolve bug. (b) a plain LIST of row objects = an uncapped, trustworthy tick: every frontend/backend/server row present (servers under the cap). The server prunes rows that disappeared from a list tick. (c) the WRAPPER object {'rows': [...], 'servers_capped': true} = a CAPPED tick: all frontend+backend rows plus the first _SERVER_CAP (400) server rows sorted problems-first. The server MUST NOT prune server-type rows on a capped tick (a server absent only because it was capped is not 'removed'); frontend/backend rows are still complete and may be pruned. (d) [] (empty list) = the stats endpoint was reachable with genuinely zero proxies -- safe to prune all rows. Dispatch: null -> skip; dict -> capped (rows = data['rows'], skip pruning servers); list -> normal (prune missing). Same null-vs-empty discipline as the zfs and php_fpm contracts.

row_contract.server: HAProxy CSV 'svname' -- 'FRONTEND' / 'BACKEND' for aggregate rows, else the server name. (proxy, server) is the per-entity key.
row_contract.type: Derived from the CSV 'type' column: 0->'frontend', 1->'backend', 2->'server'. Listener rows (type 3) and any unknown type are DROPPED (per-bind noise, out of scope for the backend-down trigger).
row_contract.status: HAProxy CSV 'status' passed through VERBATIM (UP / DOWN / MAINT / DRAIN / NOLB / 'no check' / transitional 'UP 1/3' / 'DOWN 1/2'). The server normalizes; MAINT/DRAIN MUST stay distinguishable from DOWN so maintenance never pages.
row_contract.sessions_limit: CSV 'slim' -- session limit (maxconn); null when unset.
row_contract.queue_current: CSV 'qcur' -- requests queued right now; null on rows that do not queue (frontends).
row_contract.http_4xx_total: CSV 'hrsp_4xx' -- RAW cumulative 4xx counter; the server rate()s it. Never reset or diff agent-side.
row_contract.check_status: CSV 'check_status' -- last health-check result (e.g. L4OK / L7OK / L4CON / L4TOUT); null for frontend/backend aggregate rows and no-check servers.
row_contract.check_duration_ms: CSV 'check_duration' -- last health-check duration in ms; null when no check ran.
row_contract._mapping: Columns are mapped BY HEADER NAME, never by index -- the CSV column set shifts across HAProxy versions. The fixture header interleaves unmapped columns (qmax/smax/stot/weight/rate) between the mapped ones so an index-based reader would produce garbage. Every row carries all fourteen keys with null where the column is empty/absent.
row_contract._capped_wrapper: When a tick is capped the payload is {'rows': [...], 'servers_capped': true} instead of a bare list. frontend+backend rows come first (CSV order), then the kept server rows in problems-first order.

healthy.description: Socket mode. One frontend, one backend, two UP servers. Pins the plain-list payload, the type-code -> string mapping, by-name column mapping, verbatim status, raw counters, and null on absent cells (frontend qcur/retries/check_*, backend check_*, server slim). CSV order (frontend, servers, BACKEND) is preserved.

backend_down_server_maint.description: HTTP CSV mode with basic auth. A backend is DOWN with one server DOWN (check L4CON) and one server in MAINT (check L4OK). THE DISTINGUISHABILITY GUARD: MAINT is passed through verbatim, never collapsed to DOWN, so the server can suppress paging for the maintenance server while the DOWN server and DOWN backend drive haproxy_backend_down.

zero_proxies.description: Socket mode. The stats endpoint is reachable but the CSV carries only the header (genuinely zero proxies). Emits [] so the server prunes all rows. Distinct from null: the scrape succeeded and parsed.

collection_failure.description: Socket mode where the transport yields nothing (socket refused / timed out / unparseable body). Emits null (collection failure); the server MUST NOT prune rows or resolve haproxy_backend_down incidents.

capped_tick.description: THE CAP SHARP EDGE. Three servers under one backend with _SERVER_CAP shrunk to 2 (server_cap, an agent-side test input). CSV order is [srv_up_a, srv_down, srv_up_b] but the DOWN server MUST survive the cap: the payload is the wrapper {'rows': [...], 'servers_capped': true} with frontend+backend first (always shipped), then the kept servers problems-first (srv_down ahead of the UP servers). srv_up_b is dropped. The server must skip pruning server rows on this tick.
